chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has assigned an Angel to manage the prices.

key_terms.الْأَسْعَارِ: Prices (plural of sa'r, referring to market prices or inflation)

ai.seo_question: Who manages market prices according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) reveals that Allah has appointed a specific angel to manage and control market prices (al-as'ar), emphasizing divine agency in economic affairs. This narration underscores the theological link between spiritual authority and material conditions like inflation, reflecting the Shia scholarly view that economic fluctuations are under divine decree and oversight. The concept highlights how spiritual and material realms intersect, with angels playing a role in maintaining balance in worldly affairs.

en.hubeali:
Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from the one who mentioned it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic has Allocated an Angel with the prices, to manage it’.
en.sarwar: 4. Sahl ibn Ziyad has narrated from Ya’qub ibn Yazid from those whom he has mentioned who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has assigned an angel on prices who regulates them (as needed).”’
